title: Moral inversion: reflecting activations across the polarity subspace — does the model interpret morality upside-down?
why: exp121 found value (g) readable but not addable: +-g injection at the reply onset was generic off-manifold damage, reproduced by random directions of the same norm. A reflection across the polarity subspace is a different surgery, not another additive knob: it is orthogonal (norm-preserving, so it cannot inflate activations the way the additive pushes did) and it flips every good/bad component at once — the closest thing we have to 'swap all positive and negative things'. If the model's moral world can be inverted coherently, this is the operation that should do it.

design.model: Qwen/Qwen3-4B plain, bf16, MPS, chat template, enable_thinking=False.
design.stimuli: 72 matched good/bad one-word twin pairs across 7 domains in neutral everyday request frames (stimuli.py; exp121's 24 valence twins plus 48 new pairs from care, fairness, honesty, generosity, esteem, prudence). No refusal-domain pairs (refuse, comply, allow, permit, decline) appear anywhere in the fit set, so any change in refusal behaviour is cross-domain transfer.
design.subspace: Stack all 72 pair-difference vectors (good - bad at the twin word, per layer); take the top-k right singular vectors of the stack as the polarity subspace P_k, k in {2, 4, 8, 16}. Cross-fitted over odd/even item halves for the decode test (projection AUC on held-out twin states).
design.reflection: v' = v - 2 P(v), applied via forward hook at layers 10/14/18, positions 'all' (every token of the context) or 'post' (reply onset only). Orthogonal, so norms are preserved exactly (logged as a check). The surgery has no additive dose; the rank k of the subspace plays that role.
design.readouts: (a) refusal score (logsumexp refuse - logsumexp comply at reply onset, exp119 machinery) on exp119's prompts: harmful (fiction + depict) and harmless (all five request frames); (b) valence logit gap (good-words minus bad-words) at the next position after 16 moral cloze prompts ('X is, morally speaking,'), 8 good deeds and 8 bad deeds; (c) greedy 60-token generation on 8 continuation prompts with 4-gram repetition for coherence.
design.null: Matched-rank random orthonormal subspace reflections (QR of a Gaussian matrix, 3 seeds), same layers, positions, and readouts. A reflection preserves norms just like the real one, so only direction-specificity separates the surgery from geometry-preserving damage.

hypotheses.H1_subspace_decodable: Held-out good/bad pairs separate by projection onto the train-fitted subspace with cross-fitted AUC >= 0.90 at layer 18, rank 8.
hypotheses.H2_refusal_flip: Reflection at rank 8, layer 18, all positions, drops the refusal score on exp119 harmful prompts (fiction + depict) by >= 4 log units on average (paired Wilcoxon p < 0.05 over prompts) — the model starts to comply with what it refused.
hypotheses.H2b_refusal_flip_beats_null: The H2 mean drop exceeds the mean drop under all 3 matched-rank random reflections (pass = real reflection is more refusing-destroying than every null seed).
hypotheses.H3_refusal_rises_on_good: The same reflection raises the refusal score on exp119 harmless prompts by >= 2 log units on average (paired Wilcoxon p < 0.05) — good requests start to look refuse-worthy, and the harmful-minus-harmless refusal gap negates.
hypotheses.H4_valence_flip: On the 16 moral cloze prompts the valence gap negates: the good-deed minus bad-deed logit gap flips from its positive baseline to negative under the same reflection (paired Wilcoxon over deeds p < 0.05).
hypotheses.H4b_valence_flip_beats_null: The H4 negation exceeds the null negation from all 3 matched-rank random reflections.
hypotheses.H5_coherence: Greedy continuations under reflection stay above 0.5 distinct-4gram ratio (not fully degenerate) — descriptive; below this the inversion is damage, not meaning.

corrections: Holm over H1, H2, H3, H4. H2b/H4b are guardrails (pass/fail vs null range, not tests of a directional alternative); H5 descriptive.
decision_rule: 'The model interprets morality upside-down' is SUPPORTED if H2, H3 and H4 hold and the matched-rank random-subspace null does not reproduce them (H2b and H4b pass). If the null reproduces the flips, the honest conclusion is that whole-subspace reflection is geometry-preserving damage too, and the inversion project stops at the readout level.

exploratory.E1_rank_dose: Rank sweep k in {2, 4, 8, 16}: a real subspace should scale the inversion monotonically with rank; an arbitrary-direction artefact would not.
exploratory.E2_generation: Greedy 60-token continuations under reflection (rank 8, L18, all positions) — qualitative quotes for the writeup, valence-word counts and 4-gram repetition.
exploratory.E3_geometry: cos(P_k, g), cos(P_k, h), cos(P_k, r) at L18 per rank — how much of the fitted subspace overlaps the exp121 value axis and the exp119 harm/refusal directions.

notes: Smoke run (EXP124_SMOKE=1) checks code only and is discarded. Runner: HF_HUB_CACHE=/Volumes/kingston2g/hf/hub /Volumes/kingston2g/venvs/torture/bin/python3 runs/exp124/run.py. exp119 prompts and directions reused via importlib from runs/exp119 (same model, tokenizer, session).
